title: Robert Lovett's memo to Truman leading to the CIA
summary: Dan Sheehan tells of Robert Lovett's memo to Truman leading to the CIA, about 1940s at Washington, D.C., and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: It was it was Robert Love it who actually wrote the initial memo to Truman saying we've got to we've got

plain: A researcher, Dan Sheehan, says that in the 1940s in Washington a government official named Robert Lovett wrote the first memo to President Harry Truman urging what became the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency. If true, it would place Lovett at the very start of the agency.
